descriptors.R: nominee of a new party, organized since 1854 in the free states, that would bar slavery from the territories and admit Kansas as a free state; an explorer of the Far West and briefly a senator, new to party politics
descriptors.D: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1853; a former Secretary of State and minister to Britain, abroad during the Kansas–Nebraska fight, standing on the right of each territory's settlers to decide on slavery
descriptors.O: nominee of the nativist party that would lengthen naturalization and keep the foreign-born from office, and that seeks to quiet the slavery question; a former President

compile_desc.R: the new party organized since 1854 against the extension of slavery
compile_desc.D: the party of the administration in office since 1853

others_line: Other candidates on very few ballots (answer "other").
never_name: Frémont, Buchanan, Breckinridge, Dayton, Fillmore, Donelson, Pierce, Douglas or Sumner

slice_sources.men: 1850 and 1860 censuses interpolated to November 1856, white men 21+ outside the eleven later-Confederate states; property tests had mostly ended and a few New England states let free Black men vote; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.women: No women could vote for president in 1856; women 21+ shown for population only.
slice_sources.south-white: 1850 and 1860 censuses interpolated to 1856, white adults in the eleven later-Confederate states; white men voted except in South Carolina, whose legislature chose its electors; the new free-soil party was on almost no Southern ballot; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1850 and 1860 censuses interpolated to 1856, Black adults in the eleven later-Confederate states, overwhelmingly enslaved; enslaved people could not vote and no Southern state let free Black men vote.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1850 and 1860 censuses interpolated to 1856, foreign-born white men not yet naturalized; several Western states let declarant aliens vote, elsewhere only naturalized men could.
